Rashi on Nedarim 53b:1:1.hebrew: (גמ') לא שנו - דשביעית מותר בירקות הגינה אלא במקום שאין מביאין ירק מח"ל, דכיון שאין מביאין, ודאי לא נדר אלא מאותם שמסתפקים שם, היינו מירקות השדה, ולהכי מותר בשל גינה:
Rashi on Nedarim 53b:1:1.english: (Gemara) They only taught - [that in] the Sabbatical Year one is permitted garden vegetables only in a place where they do not bring vegetables from outside the Land [of Israel]; for since they do not bring [them], he certainly vowed only against those [vegetables] that are supplied there — namely, field vegetables — and therefore he is permitted those of the garden.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:1:2.hebrew: אבל במקום שמביאין כו' אסור - אף בירקות הגינה, הואיל ורגילין לאכול שם בין ירקות השדה בין ירקות הגינה, דודאי אדעתא דהכי נדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 53b:1:2.english: However, in a place where [people] bring, etc., [he is] prohibited - Even [regarding] garden vegetables, since [people] are accustomed to eat there both field vegetables and garden vegetables, for [he] certainly vowed with this in mind.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:2:1.hebrew: כתנאי כו' - לדעתא דמ"ד אין מביאין ירקות כו', לדידיה מותר בירקות גינה ואסור בירקות שדה, דכיון דאין מביאין, לאו עליה נדר. ולמ"ד מביאין, אסור אף בירקות גינה:
Rashi on Nedarim 53b:2:1.english: Like [a dispute between] tanna'im, etc. - According to the opinion of the one who says they do not bring vegetables, etc., according to him, [the vower] is permitted [to eat] garden vegetables and prohibited [from eating] field vegetables, for since they do not bring [them from outside the Land], he did not vow regarding them. And according to the one who says they do bring [them], he is prohibited even [from eating] garden vegetables.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:2:2.hebrew: משום גוש - שמא יש מעפר חוצה לארץ בעיקרייהו, וטמא משום ספק מת:
Rashi on Nedarim 53b:2:2.english: Because of a clod - Lest there be [some] of the earth of outside the Land [of Israel] on their roots, and [it] is ritually impure due to a doubt [concerning] a corpse.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:3:1.hebrew: אסור באיספרגוס - דהוי בכלל כרוב, דמין כרוב הוא:
Rashi on Nedarim 53b:3:1.english: [He is] prohibited from [eating] ispargus - For it is included in [the category of] cabbage, since it is a type of cabbage.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:3:2.english: [He is] permitted [to eat] cabbage - For cabbage is not included in ispargus.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:4:1.english: [He is] prohibited from [eating] stew - of pounded beans.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:4:2.hebrew: מותר בגריסין - ד"ה דאין גריסין בכלל מקפה:
Rashi on Nedarim 53b:4:2.english: [He is] permitted [to eat] pounded beans - All agree that pounded beans are not included in [the category of] stew [mikpa].

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:4:3.english: From the stew - [That is made] of pounded beans.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:4:4.hebrew: אסור בשום - שנותנים ממנו בקדרה, דהיינו בכלל מקפה:
Rashi on Nedarim 53b:4:4.english: [He is] prohibited from garlic - For they put [some] of it into the pot, which is included in mikpa [stew].

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:4:5.hebrew: ר' יוסי מתיר - דקסבר אין מקפה בכלל גריסין:
Rashi on Nedarim 53b:4:5.english: Rabbi Yosei permits [it] - For he holds [that] stew [mikpa] is not included in [the category of] pounded beans.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:4:6.english: [He is] prohibited from garlic - [That is, the garlic] of the stew.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:4:7.english: [He is] permitted [to eat] stew - For stew is not included in [the category of] garlic.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:5:1.hebrew: אסור באשישים - בפת שמעורב בו קמח עדשים, דיש בכלל עדשים אשישים:
Rashi on Nedarim 53b:5:1.english: He is prohibited from [eating] ashishim - [That is,] from bread in which lentil flour is mixed, for ashishim are included in [the category of] lentils.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:5:2.english: And from ashishim, etc. - [This] is the opinion of everyone.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:6:1.hebrew: ר' יהודה אומר קונם גריס או חטה שאגי טועם מותר לכוס - חטה וגריס סתם, דלא אמר חטה חטין גריס גריסין, דקסבר [ר"י גריס או חטה] מבושלים משמע, חיין לא משמע. ור' יהודה לא פליג עליה דתנא קמא:
Rashi on Nedarim 53b:6:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: "Konam pounded bean or wheat that I taste," he is permitted to chew [them raw] - [That is, he mentioned] wheat and pounded bean unspecified, as he did not say "wheat, wheats; pounded bean, pounded beans"; for [Rabbi Yehuda] holds [that "pounded bean or wheat"] implies cooked ones, [and] does not imply raw ones. And Rabbi Yehuda does not disagree with the first Tanna.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:7:1.hebrew: אסור לאפות - דאדעתא דהכי אמר חטה, כדי לאפות, דחטה גרגיר א' משמע, ומגרגיר לא קאמר:
Rashi on Nedarim 53b:7:1.english: Prohibited from baking - For it was with this intention that he said "ḥitta", [meaning] to bake [it into bread], because "ḥitta" implies one grain, and he was not speaking of a [single] grain.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:8:1.english: Pounded bean - [This] implies [that it is] cooked.

Rashi on Nedarim 53b:8:2.english: Pounded beans - Implies raw [ones] as well.

Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:1:1.hebrew: לא שנו - דבשביעית מותר בירקות גינה משום דלא שכיחי שיאכלו ירקות גינה, אלא במקום שאין מביאין כו'. אבל במקום שמביאין — שכיח הוא ירקי גינה, ונתכוין לאסור ירקי גינה בשביעית:
Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:1:1.english: They did not teach - that in the Sabbatical Year one is permitted [to eat] garden vegetables because it is uncommon for people to eat garden vegetables, except in a place where they do not bring [vegetables], etc. However, in a place where they do bring [them] — garden vegetables are common, and he intended to prohibit garden vegetables in the Sabbatical Year.

Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:2:1.hebrew: משום גוש - דדרך הירק להיות גוש תלוי בו, וגזרו על גוש ארץ העמים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:2:1.english: Because of a clod - For it is usual for a vegetable to have a clod [of earth] attached to it, and [the Sages] decreed [ritual impurity] upon a clod [from] the land of the nations.

Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:3:1.hebrew: איספרגוס - מין כרוב הוא, ובכלל כרוב הוא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:3:1.english: Ispargus - It is a type of cabbage, and is included in [the category of] cabbage.

Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:3:2.english: [If one vows to abstain] from ispargus, he is permitted [to eat] cabbage - For other [types of] cabbage are not called ispargus.

Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:4:1.hebrew: מן הגריסין אסור במקפה של גריסין - שנקראת גריסין אף כשהן בתבשיל, אבל מן המקפה מותר בגריסין יבשין; דלא תימא דכי נדר במקפה, מן הראוי למקפה קאמר, והיינו גריסין. ולרבנן איצטריך, דאע"ג דאסרי שום כשנדר במקפה, הכא מודו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:4:1.english: "[One who vows] from pounded beans is prohibited from mikpa [stew] of pounded beans" - because it is called "pounded beans" even when they are in a cooked dish. However, [one who vows] from mikpa is permitted [to eat] dry pounded beans; so that you should not say that when he vowed [not to benefit] from mikpa, he meant [to prohibit] that which is fit for mikpa — which is pounded beans. And [this] is needed according to the Rabbis, for even though they prohibit garlic when one vows from mikpa, here they agree [that dry pounded beans are permitted].

Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:4:2.english: [One who vows] from garlic is permitted [to eat] stew - For he only intended dry garlic.

Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:5:1.hebrew: מן האשישים - פי': פסולת עדשים; מותר בעדשים, שאין העדשים נקראין אשישין. מן העדשים — אסור באשישים, שהם נקראים על שם העדשים; ור"י מתיר, דסבר דאינם בכלל עדשים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:5:1.english: From ashishim - Explanation: [this means] lentil refuse; [one who vows from ashishim] is permitted [to eat] lentils, because lentils are not called ashishim. [One who vows] from lentils is prohibited [from eating] ashishim, because they are named after lentils; and Rabbi Yosei permits [it], because he holds that they are not included in [the term] "lentils."

Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:6:1.hebrew: חטה חטין שאני טועם אסור בין בחטין בין בפת - דחיטה משמע לאפות. ומיהו בברייתא בגמ' גרסינן איפכא. ושמא טוב לפרש הכא: חטה או חיטים, גריס או גריסין — אסור בין חיין בין מבושלין; ורבי שמעין ורבי יהודה מחלקין בין חטה לחטין, גריס גריסין, כדמפרש גבי חטה חטין: "רבי יהודה אמר קונם גריס או חטה שאני טועם — מותרין לכוס חיין", דחטה וגריס משתמעי מבושלין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:6:1.english: "Ḥittah [or] ḥittin that I taste — he is prohibited both from ḥittin and from bread" - For ḥittah implies [that which is] for baking. However, in the baraita in the Gemara we have the opposite reading. And perhaps it is good to explain here [that the Mishnah means]: [if one says] ḥittah or ḥittin, [or] geris or gerisin — he is prohibited whether [they are] raw or cooked; and Rabbi Shimon [ben Gamliel] and Rabbi Yehudah distinguish between ḥittah and ḥittin, [and between] geris [and] gerisin, as [the Mishnah] explains regarding ḥittah [and] ḥittin: "Rabbi Yehudah says: Konam geris or ḥittah that I taste — they are permitted to chew raw," for ḥittah and geris imply cooked.

Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:6:2.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר גריס או חטה שאני טועם מותר לכוס חיים - מדקאמר חטה וגריס סתם, ולא אמר (חטה) חטין גריסין, קסבר [חטה גריס] מבושלין משמע, חיין לא משמע:
Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:6:2.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: "A pounded bean or wheat that I taste," he is permitted to chew [them] raw - Since he said "wheat" and "pounded bean" unqualifiedly, and did not say "(wheat) wheats [or] pounded beans," he holds that ["wheat" and "pounded bean"] imply cooked [ones], [and] do not imply raw [ones].

Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:7:1.hebrew: חטה שאני טועם מותר לאפות - דחטה לא משמע אלא חיין, חטין משמע לאפות. ורבי שמעון ורבי יהודה לא פליגי, דלתרוייהו גריס חטה מבושלין משמע ולא חיין, גריסין חטין משמע חיין אבל לא מבושלים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 53b:7:1.english: "Ḥittah that I taste," he is permitted to bake [it] - For ḥittah only implies raw [wheat], [whereas] ḥittin implies [wheat] for baking. And Rabbi Shimon [ben Gamliel] and Rabbi Yehuda do not disagree, for according to both of them, geris [and] ḥittah imply cooked and not raw, [whereas] gerisin [and] ḥittin imply raw but not cooked.
